<objective>
Deliver the "owner invites staff" slice: owner-provisioned name + 4-digit PIN profiles (no staff emails, no staff logins), PIN hashing and verification entirely inside Postgres with in-RPC authority checks, exponential backoff on wrong entries, and soft-delete lifecycle — the app-level staff identity that the device session (Plan 04) sits on top of, held in a concrete post-verify cookie.

**User story (MVP):** **As a** restaurant owner, **I want to** add my floor staff as name + PIN profiles that only I can create, **so that** each person can identify themselves on the shared tablet without me handing out email logins or exposing anyone's PIN.

Purpose: ACCT-04 in this product means the owner provisions a PIN profile directly (D-04). D-05's distinct per-staff identifier is the forward seam for future table-level attribution, made concrete here by the post-verify tablet cookie. PIN handling (D-16/17/18/19/20) is security-sensitive and must live in SECURITY DEFINER RPCs whose authority is checked in the DB, not the app layer.
Output: migration 0002 (staff_profiles + provision/verify/deactivate/list RPCs with internal authority + backoff + owner-only RLS), owner provisioning UI, the POS-style name-grid→PIN pad, and client-SDK tests for provisioning authority, direct-RPC abuse denial, and PIN backoff.

Requirements covered: ACCT-04.
</objective>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| Owner → provision RPC | Owner-supplied name/PIN crosses into a privileged insert |
| Any authenticated principal → staff RPCs | PostgREST exposes public RPCs; the in-RPC authority check is the boundary |
| Shared tablet → verify RPC | PIN attempts from a physical floor device |
| Non-owner → staff_profiles | Any member could attempt to read pin_hash |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-03-01 | Information Disclosure | staff_profiles.pin_hash | high | mitigate | NO member SELECT policy on staff_profiles; name grid served by list_staff_for_pin (id/name only); pin_hash never selectable; hashing via pgcrypto inside SECURITY DEFINER RPC (D-19); rpc-authority test asserts non-selectability |
| T-03-02 | Elevation of Privilege | provision_staff_pin / deactivate_staff_profile authority | high | mitigate | Internal `get_venue_role = 'owner'` check inside each RPC (not just the Server Action); EXECUTE revoked from anon; direct-.rpc() non-owner denial proven in tests/staff/rpc-authority.test.ts (D-04, D-22) |
| T-03-03 | Spoofing / Elevation | verify_staff_pin cross-tenant oracle + PIN brute-force | high | mitigate | Internal membership check gates verify; EXECUTE revoked from anon; exponential backoff via failed_attempts + locked_until inside verify_staff_pin (D-18) |
| T-03-04 | Elevation of Privilege | search_path hijack on SECURITY DEFINER RPCs | medium | mitigate | Every RPC declares `set search_path = ''` and fully-qualifies table refs |
| T-03-05 | Repudiation | staff action attribution | low | mitigate | Distinct per-staff identifier (created_by / staff id) stamped on writes; verified staff_profile_id held in the tablet cookie for downstream attribution (D-05) |
</threat_model>
